plan.answer: Your two points are synthetic simulation only: 20 mass % recycled PE at 26 MPa and 40 mass % at 22 MPa against your screen of 25 MPa. No processing or tensile test was performed, so these values do not describe your Identified PCRPE resin (grade to record) or Identified virgin MDPE resin (grade to record), and they cannot select a proportion. Your entered amounts and quantity basis are still blank, so remain unknown. From home you can record grades and lots, segregate and log preparation, and plan sleeve clearance. Any specimen moulding and tensile testing needs a suitable facility with a recorded process, which is unconfirmed. Keep specimen screening separate from sleeve fit, drainage observation, and future creep and weathering. When you choose a composition target for a comparison, the trial-composition balancing calculation can help plan the masses to weigh at the facility; it does not predict strength.

material_routes.title: Separate-ratio PE screen
material_routes.change: Compare two clearly separated recycled-to-virgin PE mass-percent choices in separate recorded specimen trials, holding preparation and moulding process constant.
material_routes.why: Changing only proportion while holding preparation constant may show the direction of yield shift in your lots, so measurement can guide the next choice.
steps: Record exact grades and lot IDs for both PE resins on a mass-percent basis.
Choose two separated recycled-share levels as adjustable starting choices, labelled A and B.
Confirm a suitable facility with PE moulding and tensile testing before any heating or testing.
At that facility only, mould stated specimens for A and B under one recorded process.
Test A and B separately and use measured direction to pick one ratio to carry forward.
tradeoffs: Needs outside facility time and material
Screen does not prove sleeve fit, creep or weathering
Lot change can shift results so repeat per lot
material_routes.check: Material-development screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method. This is a chosen screening threshold, not a measured planter requirement. Sleeve fit, creep and weathering targets still need to be set. Test each ratio separately with stated specimen and method; home planning cannot establish this.

material_routes.title: Lot-segregated preparation log
material_routes.change: Standardise lot segregation, storage and preparation notes per supply lot while holding ratio fixed for the comparison.
material_routes.why: Consistent preparation and lot separation may lower noise from moisture, contamination and supply differences, making the ratio comparison clearer.
steps: Segregate PCRPE and MDPE lots with labels; keep blank amounts as unknown.
Log visual condition, odour, moisture signs and sorting notes per lot.
Store dry and covered and record storage conditions.
Use the same recorded preparation for both ratio levels in the comparison.
tradeoffs: Extra handling and storage space at home
Facility may still see gels or odour differences
material_routes.check: Preparation log with lot IDs, visual, moisture and sorting notes plus facility processing notes per level; kept separate from the tensile screen and without assuming contamination-free resin.

engineering_routes.title: Vented clearance sleeve
engineering_routes.change: Make the sleeve an outer decorative shell with deliberate clearance, draft and vent gap around the separate watertight liner that carries soil and water.
engineering_routes.why: Clearance and venting may ease fit and removal despite shrinkage and lot variation, while liner keeps load separate from the tensile screen.
steps: Measure liner diameter, height and base at home and record them.
Sketch sleeve inside size with deliberate side and base clearance plus vent gap as adjustable choices.
Use a flat paper template at home to check footprint and clearance only; it does not test drainage.
Plan vent/drain path in the real geometry to avoid trapped water.
At a suitable facility only, make real geometry and observe fit, removal and visible condition.
tradeoffs: Larger footprint than a tight sleeve
Still needs real sleeve and liner to check fit
engineering_routes.check: Fit, removal, standing and ventilation observation with real sleeve plus liner; short outdoor notes guide design only and do not establish weathering, and are separate from the specimen tensile screen.

engineering_routes.title: Two-part tolerant sleeve
engineering_routes.change: Use a two-panel sleeve with overlap or slot as an adjustable design choice to tolerate dimensional shift between lots and builds.
engineering_routes.why: Adjustable overlap may absorb shrinkage variation without requiring tight material control first.
steps: Sketch two panels as an adjustable choice with recorded overlap and fastening or slot idea.
Keep liner size and sleeve clearance recorded with each overlap setting.
Check footprint with paper template only for clearance planning.
Make real panels only at a suitable facility with confirmed moulding capability.
Record which overlap setting was used for each fit trial.
tradeoffs: Needs confirmed moulding and assembly capability
engineering_routes.check: Repeat assembly, fit and removal with real geometry across lots and builds; fit does not prove strength, retention or weathering and stays separate from specimen results.

history.content: How can I use this variable input to make the product within my targets? Propose practical material and engineering adjustments.

From home you can record grades and lots, segregate material, and plan sleeve clearance, while moulding and tensile testing need a suitable facility with a recorded process — that capability is unconfirmed. Try separate recorded PE ratios for the screen of tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method, and keep those specimen results separate from sleeve fit checks. Because your liner supports soil and water, a clearance sleeve with ventilation gap may ease fit despite lot variation. No route guarantees the screen; measurement at a facility is needed to find out which ratio, preparation and geometry to carry forward.
Material route: Record grades and test separate PE ratios. Adjust recycled-to-virgin PE proportion across separate recorded trials, holding preparation constant. Changing only the PE ratio while holding preparation constant may show the direction of yield shift in your resins, so measurement can guide the next choice. Next check: Moulded specimens tested for tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using a stated specimen and method; compare to this screen without transferring published specimen values to your resin.
Material route: Lot-aware preparation and storage plan. Standardise preparation, lot segregation and storage within allowed preparation. Consistent preparation and lot separation may lower noise from moisture, contamination and supply differences, making the ratio comparison clearer. Next check: Preparation log and visual/moisture/contamination notes per lot plus specimen yield for a fixed ratio; do not assume the resin is contamination-free.
Engineering route: Clearance sleeve around watertight liner. Adjust sleeve geometry to an outer decorative shell with deliberate clearance, draft and ventilation gap; liner continues to carry soil and water. Clearance and vented form may reduce reliance on tensile value for fit and removal, since load stays with the liner while tensile is still screened separately. Next check: Fit, removal and standing with the real sleeve plus watertight liner, plus drainage/ventilation and visible-condition observation; short outdoor notes do not establish weathering and are separate from tensile screening.
Engineering route: Tolerant build with recorded process. Use tolerant construction and a written process record to absorb shrinkage and lot variation. Adjustable fit plus lot-linked records may help see whether a fit shift follows ratio, lot or preparation, without requiring tight material control first. Next check: Repeat dimensional fit and assembly/removal across lots and builds with real geometry; keep separate from specimen tensile results and do not use fit to claim strength or durability.

Keep specimen tensile screening separate from sleeve fit, drainage observation and future creep and weathering checks.
